items.title: Printing credits, $62.50 a semester
items.renew: Credits roll over fall to spring but are wiped at the end of the academic year.
items.note: Free black-and-white printing credit every semester. The library itself has no printers - go across the 6th-floor hall to the IT suite. Colour and overage come off your Ram Card.

items.title: The New York Times, free
items.renew: Re-register every year from your signup date.
items.note: Full digital access on a joint Moakley and Sawyer subscription. Register with your @suffolk.edu address. The confirmation email usually lands in spam.

items.title: The Wall Street Journal, free
items.note: Suffolk has its own registration URL. Sign up with your Suffolk email.

items.title: The Washington Post, free
items.note: Available through Suffolk. The registration path is less clearly documented than the Times or the Journal - ask the research desk if it balks.

items.title: Headspace, free for every Suffolk student
items.note: The full app subscription, enrolled through Suffolk. The library surfaces it alongside Counseling Services and Suffolk CARES.

items.title: Discounted MBTA passes
items.note: Semester transit passes at a student rate through the Ram Card office.

items.title: Lexis+ AI (Protege)
items.note: Suffolk licenses it. Open it from the left sidebar of the Lexis+ homepage. Drafts, summarises, compares documents, generates deposition questions. Prompts are not used to train models and prompt history auto-deletes at 90 days.

items.title: CoCounsel and Ask Practical Law AI
items.note: Both licensed. Use the product switcher at the top left of the Westlaw homepage. Research, document review with citation links, timeline extraction.

items.title: The library's own guidance on AI fabrications
items.note: Read this before you rely on any of the above. It explains why Lexis+ AI and CoCounsel behave differently from raw ChatGPT, and carries Suffolk's actual rules on verification and confidential information.

items.title: Study rooms, 20 of them
items.note: Floors 5 to 7. Book 30 minutes to 4 hours, up to 7 days ahead; the day releases at 12:01am. QR check-in on the wall is required, no earlier than 30 minutes before and no later than 30 after. Repeated no-shows suspend booking.

items.title: Where you're allowed to take a Zoom call
items.note: The whole 6th floor except the reading room, plus the collaborative area at the top of the 7th-floor stairs. Headphones required.

items.title: Free scanning
items.note: Library scanners send straight to email or cloud storage at no charge.

items.title: Course reserves, 2-hour checkout
items.note: Required and recommended books for your courses. Search by professor surname or course title. If yours is missing, email your syllabus to law_circulation@suffolk.edu and they will get it.

items.title: Your first two weeks of reading, scanned to Canvas
items.note: Some professors send the library their opening readings to scan and post, so you don't need the casebook on day one. Opt-in by professor - email law_circulation@suffolk.edu to ask about yours.

items.title: Interlibrary loan
items.note: Books, chapters and articles from other institutions. Course reserves and ebooks cannot be requested. Cost and turnaround are not published.

items.title: Borrowing at seven other Boston campuses
items.note: Your Suffolk ID checks out circulating books at Simmons, Emerson, Lesley, Emmanuel, MassArt, Wentworth and Berklee through the Fenway Library Organization.

items.title: What the library will not lend you
items.note: No laptops, no chargers, no cables. It does have a few USB connections, headphones and assistive reading equipment. Chargers come from IT across the hall.

items.title: Research librarians
items.note: Desk staffed Monday to Thursday 10-6 and Friday 10-5. 617-573-8516, lawref@suffolk.edu, live chat, or book an appointment. The library itself is open 8am-11pm weekdays and 9am-11pm weekends.

items.title: The free book shelf
items.note: The library doesn't take donations but keeps a shelf of free books to take.

items.title: iCompete Writing
items.note: One of the most comprehensive collections of law student writing competitions anywhere - over 100 entries by date and topic, prizes up to $25,000. Built and maintained by Suffolk's own LPS program and the law library.

items.title: Perma.cc accounts
items.note: Link-rot-proof permanent citations. The library issues accounts only to law review writers and faculty RAs. Write-on competitors use the placeholder [PERMALINK] instead.

items.title: Past faculty exams
items.note: Real exams from Suffolk professors, searchable, and not the same set as what is on Canvas. Suffolk login required off campus.

items.title: CLE while you're still a student
items.note: MCLE OnlinePass gives you MCLE's CLE programming. Massachusetts has no mandatory CLE requirement, so this is for the material, not for credit hours.

absent.title: WordRake
absent.note: Suffolk was the first law school in the country to give students WordRake, but the licence was not renewed for 2026-27. Library FAQ 424561 still describes the annual renewal, so it is worth knowing before you email the research desk about it.

absent.title: Quimbee
absent.note: No Suffolk subscription. Zero hits across all 101 databases. Use West Academic's study aids and CALI instead.

absent.title: Aspen Learning Library
absent.note: No Suffolk subscription. The entire commercial study-aid spend is West Academic.

absent.title: Bloomberg Law
absent.note: The subscription ended June 30, 2021 and the page for it now 404s. Sawyer Library does still have a Bloomberg financial terminal.

absent.title: BARBRI or Themis bar prep
absent.note: No institutional subscription. BARBRI appears only as a sign-in provider for West Academic.

absent.title: Free PACER
absent.note: The library states plainly that it does not provide it. Use CourtLink inside your Lexis account for federal and state dockets.

absent.title: E-discovery or practice-management software
absent.note: No Relativity, Everlaw, Logikcull, Clio, HotDocs or Documate through the library. Legal tech at Suffolk means Lexis+ AI and CoCounsel.

absent.title: An institutional ChatGPT or Claude licence
absent.note: Not through the library. Its own student guide tells you to make a free personal account.
